chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim from Abu Khadija from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: Linen was for the Children of Israel — they would shroud [their dead] with it — while cotton is for the community of Muhammad (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family).
So this report does not contradict [what has been previously established].

key_terms.أُمَّةِ: ummah — the community/nation (here: the community of Muhammad SAWW)
key_terms.الْقُطْنُ: cotton (the prescribed shroud fabric for the Muslim ummah)
key_terms.الْكَتَّانُ: linen (the shroud fabric historically used by Bani Israel)
key_terms.يُكَفِّنُونَ: to shroud/wrap the dead (the act of preparing the kafan)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the correct burial shroud material for Muslims as distinguished from the practice of Bani Israel?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes the burial shroud materials of Bani Israel and the community of Muhammad (SAWW): linen was the shrouding fabric of Bani Israel, while cotton is designated for the Muslim ummah. The concluding phrase is an editorial note by Sheikh al-Tusi, signalling that this narration — though it mentions both fabrics — does not contradict the chapter's ruling that cotton alone is the prescribed shroud material.
